key_insight: Positional disorder in realistic resonant dipole-dipole interacting networks can strongly localize excitations, even though the coupling is partially long-ranged and radiative.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a route to control exciton transport and trap energy in quantum/optical devices relevant to coherent photovoltaics, quantum memory, and quantum sensors.
method: Modeled disordered spin/atom networks with realistic resonant dipole-dipole interaction (RDDI).
Analyzed the competition between coherent exchange and dissipative radiative coupling.
Identified a wavelength-dependent transition from extended to localized excitation dynamics.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical analysis showing strong localization emerging from positional disorder and interference effects in open RDDI geometries.
watch_item: Because the localization mechanism depends on realistic dipole coupling, disorder, and wavelength, device behavior may be highly sensitive to geometry and operating frequency.
paper_title: Quantum state localization in dipole-dipole interacting disordered networks
